name: zapier-calle
title: Zapier CALL-E integration
description: Zapier Platform CLI integration that places CALL-E phone calls, waits for the terminal outcome through a Zapier callback URL, and returns a fail-closed disposition alongside the transcript, summary, and structured result.

entrypoints.name: Place Call and Wait for Outcome

side_effects: Creates one outbound phone call per Zap run when Dry Run is false, a valid CALL-E API key is connected, and an authorized E.164 phone number is supplied.
safety: Dry Run returns a masked preview, never generates a Zapier callback URL, and sends no request to CALL-E.
Requires E.164 phone numbers and never infers region or locale from the number.
Derives the Idempotency-Key from a SHA-256 digest of the canonical call payload, excluding the per-run webhook URL, so an edited retry cannot replay an older call.
Classifies every outcome fail-closed: unrecognized statuses and event types resolve to needs_human, never to a successful disposition.

Judges whether an extracted structured_result is usable, not merely present. A required field that came back as an unknown-like value (unknown, unclear, not_stated, undetermined), as null or empty, or that was never returned at all, resolves to review_required rather than confirmed - even when CALL-E reports task_completed with a high confidence label. This matters because CALL-E's own schema guidance tells authors to include an unknown enum value for calls that cannot produce evidence, and the sibling calle-script-advisor skill lints for it, so the value is expected to appear on a call that reached no answer. Booleans and zeros are treated as real answers, never as absences. The create actions check against the caller's own result_schema required list; the trigger and search, which observe calls placed anywhere, check the values they can see but cannot detect a missing field.

Enforces a minimum numeric completion_confidence.score, defaulting to 0.6 and configurable per action, so a high confidence label carrying a low score is sent to review. CALL-E declares score as required and bounded 0-1 while label is documented only by example, making the label the looser field. An unparseable threshold falls back to the default rather than disabling the check; an explicit 0 disables it deliberately.

Detects a revocation of consent spoken during the call by scanning the recipient's transcript turns, and never the agent's own script, which routinely contains the opt-out disclosure that state bot-disclosure laws encourage. A detected revocation overrides the business outcome: the call is reported as needs_human with lead_state blocked_compliance and is never actionable, regardless of how well the call otherwise went, and the quote and its offset into the call are surfaced so a human can verify it and add the number to a Do Not Call List. The FCC revocation rule accepts a request made by any reasonable means and requires it to be honored within 10 days. This is a phrase list over English text, not intent classification, and its ceiling is documented in lib/opt-out.js. Because this check reads the transcript out of the recipients array, a payload whose recipients are present but not readable as a list downgrades an otherwise-confirmed call to review_required rather than reporting opt_out_requested false: a check that silently examined nothing must not produce an actionable result.

Refuses to dial when a caller-supplied history of previous attempt timestamps shows the call would exceed a per-day cap (default 2) or a minimum interval between attempts (default 4 hours), reported as its own disposition, retry_policy_blocked. The history is stateless - supplied fresh on each call, never stored - because a Zapier action has no durable storage. An unparseable or future-dated history fails closed and refuses to dial. Like the calling-window guard and unlike suppression, a dry run previews the verdict instead of being blocked by it.

Projects the ten dispositions onto three coarse states in a lead_state field - qualified, needs_human, blocked_compliance - so a no-code workflow can branch without re-deriving which values are safe to act on. Only confirmed maps to qualified; an unrecognized disposition maps to needs_human, never to qualified.

Surfaces the recipient's last spoken turn, with its offset into the call, as review_excerpt on any result that is not confirmed, so a human approval step shows the line that caused the doubt. The CALL-E API exposes no call recording or audio, so a timestamped transcript excerpt is the closest available equivalent.
Distinguishes outcome_unknown from failed so an ambiguous result does not trigger a second call.
Rejects a resumed callback whose call id does not match the call the step started.

Refuses to dial outside a configured calling window: when Recipient Timezone (IANA) is set, both create actions check the recipient's local hour (and optionally block Sunday) before any request is sent to CALL-E, and Place Call and Wait for Outcome never generates a Zapier callback URL for a call it refused. The timezone is never inferred from the phone number, region, or locale, and a raw UTC offset is rejected rather than accepted, per this repository's design-principles.md. This refusal is reported as its own disposition, outside_calling_window, distinct from the seven dispositions a completed call can produce - it fires before dialing and deriveDisposition never returns it - so a downstream Zap can tell a policy refusal apart from any outcome of an actual call. A dry run is never blocked by this guard: it always returns its masked preview, with a calling_window object reporting what the live path would have decided, so a Zap can be previewed at any hour.
Masks phone numbers in previews, outputs, and error messages.
Does not create recurring schedules; Zapier owns scheduling.

The Call Completed trigger is an unauthenticated static webhook: CALL-E has no webhook subscription API to verify a delivery against, so a forged POST to a discovered URL is indistinguishable from a real CALL-E event at the transport layer. It fails closed on malformed payloads (returns no result rather than throwing) and reuses the same disposition classifier as the create actions and search, but does not authenticate the caller; downstream Zaps should branch on disposition and must not treat correlation_id as proof of origin.

Refuses to dial a number on a caller-supplied Do Not Call List: both create actions check the recipient's number, digits-only and formatting-insensitive, against an optional per-call suppression list before any request is sent to CALL-E, and Place Call and Wait for Outcome never generates a Zapier callback URL for a call it refused this way. The list is stateless - supplied fresh on each call, never stored by this integration - and a list that cannot be read as text fails closed as suppressed rather than risking a dial. Unlike the calling-window guard, a dry run does not preview for a suppressed number, since suppression is about the number itself rather than timing. This refusal is reported as its own disposition, suppressed, distinct from the other nine - it fires before dialing and deriveDisposition never returns it.
credentials: CALL-E API key stored in the Zapier connection as a password-typed field.
